experiment.claim: Issue #9 (error-amplifier design to an offset/mismatch budget). Substantiates the deterministic half of that issue's acceptance criteria for design/error_amp.sch closing the loop around design/bandgap_core.sch: (a) loop stability -- DC loop gain, unity-gain frequency, phase margin and gain margin over the full PVT matrix; (b) the Kuijk offset gain dVOUT/dVOS that design/error-amp-offset-budget.md converts an input-referred offset into an output error with, measured rather than taken from the idealized (1 + R2/R1) algebra; (c) PSRR at DC against the > 60 dB line; (d) the < 50 uA Iq budget, split into the amplifier's share and the core's share. The RANDOM half of the budget (sigma(VOS) from local mismatch) is a distribution claim and lives in sim/error-amp-offset-mc/; the +/-1% untrimmed output-accuracy spec line over PVT is issue #11's experiment, not this one.
experiment.statistical_convention: N/A (corner-matrix claim; the distribution claim is sim/error-amp-offset-mc/)
experiment.title: Error amplifier in its bandgap loop: stability, offset gain, PSRR and Iq split over PVT

spread_checks.note: Guards against a silently corner-blind harness: VEB moves ~2 mV/degC, so a -40..125 degC sweep must move this by >150 mV. If every corner returns the same value, the .lib/.temp injection is not reaching the simulator.
The stability number itself must move across the matrix. A phase margin identical on all 45 points would mean the AC probe is reading something corner-independent (i.e. not the circuit).
